title: Installed applications (system-wide)
whyItMatters: The launcher entries list what is installed on the machine. On its own that is a profile of the person's tools and interests, and it shows what a new owner will find in the menu.
source: freedesktop.org Desktop Entry spec plus the FHS location /usr/share/applications for system-wide entries: https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/
notes: Names only. Packages without a launcher entry, snap and Flatpak exports installed elsewhere, and console-only tools do not appear here.

steps: Open App Center from the desktop application menu.
Go to its list of installed applications.
Choose Uninstall for each app you no longer need; an administrator password is required.
cleanup.risk: Removes selected system applications and their desktop launchers from the operating system.
cleanup.source: Ubuntu Desktop Guide, Remove an application: https://web.archive.org/web/20240313160743/https://help.ubuntu.com/stable/ubuntu-help/addremove-remove.html
